findings.title: i18next placeholders replaced with Java MessageFormat syntax breaks the account console message
findings.body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. This bundle is consumed by the React account console through i18next, whose interpolation syntax is double braces (see every other entry in this file, e.g. `error-invalid-length-too-short='{{0}}' must have minimal length of {{1}}.`). With single braces none of the arguments are substituted and the ICU/MessageFormat choice construct is not supported by i18next either, so the user will literally see `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` instead of the attribute name and the allowed bounds. If pluralization is desired here it has to be done with i18next plural keys (`_one`/`_other`), as already done for `resourceSharedWith_one`/`_other`.

findings.title: i18next placeholders replaced with Java MessageFormat syntax breaks the admin console message
findings.body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The `maven-resources` admin bundle is loaded by the admin console via i18next, which only interpolates `{{...}}` placeholders and does not understand MessageFormat `choice` constructs. The rendered error will therefore show the raw format string instead of the attribute name and the min/max limits, making the validation error useless for the administrator. Only the server-side bundles (`themes/.../theme/base/*/messages/*`) are formatted with `java.text.MessageFormat` and may use single braces/choice.

findings.title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: `totpStep1` is now `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The same wrong string was introduced in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` (`loginTotpStep1`, line 71). Lithuanian users will see an Italian sentence in the OTP setup screens. Either translate the new wording or drop the key so the English fallback is used.

findings.title: Traditional Chinese text added to the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) bundle
findings.body: `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese characters/terminology (手機, 應用程式) and appears to be copied from the zh_TW bundle. All other entries in this zh_CN file are Simplified Chinese (手机, 应用). Simplified-Chinese users will see mixed script on the OTP setup page.

findings.title: Missing English counterpart aborts the build with a bare RuntimeException
findings.body: The English reference bundle is derived purely by string surgery on the absolute path (`replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")` plus `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`). If the derived file does not exist – e.g. a community-only theme/message directory that has no counterpart under `resources`, a bundle whose file name does not follow the `_<locale>.properties` convention, or a future directory rename – the code throws an unchecked `RuntimeException("unable to read file ...")` from inside the `forEach`/verify path. That bypasses the `MojoExecutionException` contract of `verify()` and fails the whole build with a raw stack trace instead of a readable validation message. The missing-English case should either be skipped (treat as "no HTML allowed", as `getEnglishValue` already does for missing keys) or reported via `MojoExecutionException` with guidance.

findings.title: Diff trimming can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException while building the error message
findings.body: The two while-loops compute a common prefix length (`start`) and a common suffix length (`end`) independently, so `start + end` can exceed the length of the shorter string. Example: value `abb`, sanitized `ab` gives start=2 and end=2, and `value.substring(2, 3 - 2)` → `substring(2, 1)` throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` (the same happens on the `sanitized.substring(...)` call for value `aa`/sanitized `a`). This happens exactly when a violation has been detected, so instead of reporting the offending key the plugin aborts the build with an unrelated exception and the real problem is hidden. Clamp with e.g. `end = Math.min(end, Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start)`.

findings.title: Anchor-mismatch message omits file and key, and the `key` parameter is unused
findings.body: `messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string")` gives no indication of which properties file or which message key failed, unlike the HTML message a few lines above which includes both. Since the plugin is run over hundreds of bundles, a failure produces an unactionable message. The method already receives `key` but never uses it; include `key` and `file` in the text (and reword "original string" to something like "in the English source value").

findings.title: Byte-exact comparison against the sanitizer output rejects semantically identical HTML
findings.body:
The check is `!Objects.equals(sanitized, value)`, i.e. the translation must match the sanitizer's *serialization* exactly, not just be free of disallowed markup. The OWASP sanitizer always emits void elements as `
`, so a perfectly safe `
` is flagged as "Illegal HTML" – which is why this PR has to rewrite `
` to `
` in ~20 translation files. Every future translation contribution (including machine/Weblate imports) that writes `
`, `
`, extra whitespace inside a tag, etc. will fail the build with a confusing "Illegal HTML" diff even though nothing unsafe is present. Consider comparing a canonicalized form of both sides (e.g. sanitize the value twice and compare the two sanitizer outputs) so only real policy violations are reported.

findings.title: Property bundles are read as ISO-8859-1 while the files are UTF-8
findings.body: `new PropertyResourceBundle(FileInputStream)` loads the file with `Properties.load(InputStream)`, which decodes ISO-8859-1, whereas `verifyNoDuplicateKeys` reads the same file with `Files.readString` (UTF-8). Keycloak theme message bundles are UTF-8, so every non-ASCII value is mojibake inside the sanitizer check and, more importantly, in the reported "Illegal HTML in key ..." messages, which makes failures for Arabic/Chinese/Cyrillic bundles very hard to read. Use `new PropertyResourceBundle(new InputStreamReader(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8))`.

findings.title: No negative test and weakened assertions hide false positives
findings.body:
The assertions were relaxed from `Matchers.contains` to `Matchers.hasItem`, so a test now passes even if the verifier emits additional, unexpected messages. Combined with the fact that there is no test asserting an *empty* result for a legitimate file (e.g. a `_de` bundle whose English source contains ``/`

`/`
` and whose translation uses the same allowed tags, or a bundle containing `{{0}}` placeholders and `{N,choice,...}` constructs), the suite cannot detect the false positives this checker is most likely to produce – which is exactly the risk that forced the large number of cosmetic edits in this PR. Add a test asserting `verify()` returns an empty list for a valid translation.
